Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

In addition, please don't ever put the full text of a draft in a forum post: if you wish to share the draft, the best method is to create a Sandbox Page for it so you can share a link to the draft instead.

item.title: Draft: The Holly King: Re: Draft: The Holly King
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I am…somewhat torn on this as a whole. There's a lot of charm to it that I like, but it feels a touch unsatisfying as a whole, I think in part because the interview doesn't necessarily go very far and really just serves to convey more about what the SCP is: it feels like this is a whole thing built on the mystery of who the SCP is and in turn the reveal of them being santa, and unfortunately I was lurking in #thecritters when grigori asked about that so I figured it out pretty soon.

I think it works as a whole though, and I would likely upvote this but?

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

No other measures are necessary to successfully and safely contain him in his current state

I'm not necessarily sure that 'successfully' and 'safely' are both necessary here; safely contain to me implies successful but?

SCP-XXX is considered a nomenclative hazard (Eshu Class).

Something like "SCP-XXXX is an Eshu Class nomenclative hazard" might read better here; even if this is the phrasing SCP-4000 uses to refer to it.

However, previous attempts to contain SCP-XXXX per protocol 4000-Eshu have been deemed inadequate.

My personal preference would be for this to continue with e.g. "due to [reason]", namely, where the reasons it's been deemed inadequate are in some way shown.

I'd also lean towards capitalising protocol here and in the next sentence but it's largely a stylistic thing so w/e.

As an additional measure, the entrance of cell B5 is to be reinforced with iron.

I'd lean towards including this as a paragraph on it's own? It feels like it doesn't quite flow from the previous stuff but?

These alterations have been marked for differentiation from the standard formatting.

My personal preference here would be to explicitly say 'marked in blue' over making it blue, though I think it's clear enough without?

SCP-XXXX has knowledge of the name, middle name (if any), and surnames of all people it comes into contact with.

I feel like '…knowledge of the full name of all…' would be clearer, with like, middle/surnames being possibly mentioned in a footnote; though that feels unnecessary.

access granted

I'd probably capitalise this (Access Granted).

SCP-XXX was discovered during a performance of the 4000-Halloway procedure.

Minor note but this placeholder has only 3 X's so I'd probably add an extra just to ensure you don't miss it when changing the placeholder into a number.

which resulted in the appearance of SCP-XXXX in the chimney rather than an entrance to the the place of the nameless oddities.

this phrasing is a little ambiguous as to whether you mean "SCP-XXXX should have appeared in the entrance to the place of the nameless oddities but instead appeared in the chimney" or (more likely) "the entrance to the place of the nameless oddities should have appeared but instead SCP-XXXX appeared in the chimney"

This is believed to be due to the cultural association toof the epithet in question.

The following is an interview conducted on June 20th 1996.

This date is meaningless to us because we don't know when it is in relation to the discovery of the SCP: it could be two days later, it could be two hundred years later or it could be thirty days before.

however two members of security personnel were present beside the chamber entrance for emergency assistance

SCP-XXXX, I actually came to ask you a few questions. We want to know how you differ from the others like you.

Addressing the SCP directly here like this feels a little odd: like, there's only two people in the room, so it seems unnecessary for her to do this?

I see now, I see, you mean ██████.

See, this feels like it's hiding 'Santa' but it's a letter too long for that so I'm not sure if I'm wrong or this is a mistake?

Well, this clearly isn't the case for you, SCP-XXXX.

But, one makes duedo if they areone is to survive.

they to one here to keep the pronoun consistent

SCP-XXXX laughs

SCP-XXXX: I don't believe I ever said such a thing

Okay so this visually appears like it has an extra line but reading the page source, it's that none of the others do properly, probably because one of your ">"'s doesn't have a space after it?

(It's generally easier to wrap long things like this between "[[div class="blockquote"]]" and "[[/div]]", since it doesn't have awkward stuff like this)

Footnote 5. holly

I'd capitalise holly here

[-] Line By Line

item.title: SCP *PLACE HOLDER NUMBER* The Bee movie.: SCP *PLACE HOLDER NUMBER* The Bee movie.
item.content:encoded:
For context before we get into the meat of this thread, I was inspired to write this because I've often heard the bee movie be described as a collective fever dream, I feel like it could fit into the joke scp category, but I think with more tweaking it could be a full fledged article.

Scp 9999 The Bee movie.

Object class: Safe.

Special containment procedures:

Due to the circumstances surrounding SCP 9999 full scale containment as of this moment is both impossible and unnecessary. Personnel are instead instructed to avoid viewing SCP 9999, MTF-PHI 22 “Fever Dreamers” is to be alerted to any devices reported to contain a recording of SCP 9999, recordings are to be either destroyed or given directly to Director McKinley for [DATAEXPUNGED]. If any personnel should happen to view SCP 9999 they are instructed to avoid telling others about it or posting about it on social media in order to attempt to slow the spread of its anomalous effects.

Description:

SCP 9999 is the official designation for a viral phenomenon which causes the victim to hallucinate having viewed a computer animated movie from 2007 called The Bee Movie which stars comedian Jerry Seinfeld. Those affected usually have wildly different experiences in regards to SCP 9999, with some reporting that the film they watched was a romantic comedy, while others report that the film they watched was a surreal horror film, in spite of this however four factors remain constant.

Number one: the main character is always voiced by Jerry Seinfeld.

Number two: the main character will attempt to sue the human race over their consumption of honey.

Number three: the love interest of the main character will always be human.

Number four: the film will always end with The main character and the love interest opening a joined flower shop/law firm.

Although the foundation has managed to create a ‘dummy film’ and amnestise most of those who have been affected by SCP 9999, there remain a few affected individuals who further propagate the effects of SCP 9999.

item.title: any suggestions to make my SCP look better?: Re: any suggestions to make my SCP look better?
item.content:encoded:
Feedback
Read Below

A couple things here:

The entire page should be looked over for punctuation errors. Capitalization, commas, etc. It breaks immersion seeing a Foundation researcher write;

"by singing the song take on me by aha"

It should be:

"By singing the song Take On Me by Aha."

Revision 5159-A should be capitalized, and I highly recommend it is put in a quote box to separate it from the rest of the page.

- Audio from Skimmers radio during investigation

You should add who Skimmers is, before the log. I don't know if he is a government agent, an MTF officer, a scientist, etc. Example:

MTF Agent dispatched: Skimmers, John
Time: 0500 Dec 16, 2020
Reason for dispatch: Unknown anomalous presence

This gives more clarity on who he is. Remember, the Foundation documents basically everything. They are trying to study these things, and these documents are looked back upon for research in the future.

Interviewer: do you have a name?

SCP-5159: Yes, my name is Joseph Walker.

Here personally I don't think the Foundation really cares what his name is. They view him as an anomaly, not as a person. Staff are often very cold with the SCPs unless there is an anomalous or memetic reason not to be.

Also don't forget your rating module. A common mistake.

Other than that, good job.

item.title: First SCP Draft: Re: First SCP Draft
item.content:encoded:
Hmmmm, the ways that the alter-Bens try to improve Ben ultimately are harmful to Ben's mental and at some points physical health. The other him do know this and therefore the worst-case scenario could involve Ben being completely disheartened by this and thinking that he can't improve at all and that these alternate versions of him are simply better than him/he doesn't feel like he can get to the points that all of them reached in their lives. Either way he gives up on trying to improve himself and falls back into a state of despair and spirals downwards thinking about his place in the world when so many other, better, versions of him exist.

Something like that could be the worst-case scenario, but I'm not quite sure how I would convey that idea in the story. Would he show doubt about his own abilities and keep comparing himself to them? Which they encourage more and more until he realises they aren't good for him? I don't know how I would go about that. But if any of that sounded like a good idea I could give it a shot.

item.title: Your Personal Hell: Re: Your Personal Hell
item.content:encoded:
Holdplacer

I see what you were aiming for here, which itself is a very good sign. The message of karmic justice comes across clearly, as does the imagery, all good things.

That being said, the last test with the O5 kind of threw me for a loop? What was done is redacted, which leaves a lot up to interpretation for the reader. To remedy this, I would suggest listing some of what they've done and redacting the rest. It'll give us the impression that the stuff that's been left in is less intense(?) than what was left out. It will also sort of guide us a bit more, which can help make the ending more impactful depending on what you allude to.

I'm also left wondering if these people will eventually die or not. In the case of Patrick Cain, sausages made from his body are produced every so often. Eventually the man will run out of body to be used, despite being immortal. A bit of clarity here would really help set the mood. If they're all immortal but still susceptible to bodily harm (a la the end of death canon), then they'll habe a different type of pain than if they were immortal and constantly regenerating.

A spherical zone with a radius of two metres centered on White transformed into an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 while he was delivering a sermon in church.

This seems contradictory to the conditions the akomaly requires to manifest. He's in the midsts of giving a sermon, so there are other people around him, yes? By the description of the anomaly, he shouldn't have been affected. The spherical zone is also not condusive with the rest of the article. Every other test takes place in physical rooms of some sort, yet Albert White does not?

Unless I am misunderstanding the image here, this is the omly inconsistency with the tests.

I think that's all I have for you. Good luck!

item.title: Dysphoric Flesh: Re: Dysphoric Flesh
item.content:encoded:
Oops I forgot I had placeholdered this yesterday until I went to bed but I have uh just managed to not go over 24hrs too much

[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I'm a little conflicted on this as a whole: the final few paragraphs have this really delightful rising sense of dread that works for me in a really dark way that I really dig; but it feels…like the ending just kinda…happens? I was originally going to highlight this just appearing in wombs as being an issue:

SCP-XXXX may manifest in the wombs of women who have undergone menopause and are the parent of adult children who currently identify as transgender or non-binary

But I think it could be worked better into the ending: it feels, like you'd have this great opportunity for like…the SCP-XXXX instance to crumble into dust and emit more parasites and have like, the -1 instances really like…come together to crow about how good a job they did protecting their kid from being trans and like, regretting that being trans killed their kid while the narrative here is very framed around the mothers being more responsible?

It's a hard balance: in some ways, the ending resulting in more spread of this feels like it'd be more narratively satisfying but it also feels like it might really impact the kinda…broad impact that it currently has; where like, at the moment it affects basically every trans person. But I feel like the specific horror might outweigh that: in that, having it feel like a kinda localised, spreading phenomenon would help make this feel more real and hence more impactful?

I'm also kinda iffy about this starting in the mother at all as a thing; it feels…underutilised? Like a lot of the horror comes more from peoples reactions to this happening to -2, and so it feels like the instances originally being from the mother feels almost tangential?

There's some pacing issues: it kinda feels like the start of the description drags stuff out a lot in a very dry way; and it feels more concisely moving to the actual meat of this would land better.

There's a small part of me that feels like this needs more than a light touch up at the end: I can see like, a longer form diary or series of interviews say having a much larger effect here; but it feels like they might really struggle to show anything new that the description already implies, and I don't necessarily think having a big focus on a specific mother/child relation here would actually be the best way to do this.

Speaking here from a sensitivity perspective alone: I don't think this has issues with that specifically; though there's definitely points where it feels like this is going to be really bad in that regard. I think tying the detransitioning stuff into people's reactions, and in turn, the eventual death into exclusively people being unsupportive works. I…am hesitant only in that this feels…miserable? It's very much a piece about despair and the loss of hope and while I personally think that it's done in a way which works, I can see people disagreeing and I would suggest reaching out to a few other trans/non-binary critters about this.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

openly transgender and non-binary individuals for signs of SCP-XXXX activity.

I'm, not necessarily a fan of 'signs of SCP-XXXX activity' here: on the one hand, keeping it open for any kind of sign like this is probably good for ConProcs; but it feels like this is a really great moment for you to imply something specific to hook a reader in; perhaps 'for signs of parasitic infection by SCP-XXXX' or perhaps something more specific.

SCP-XXXX is then to be surgically removed from SCP-XXXX-2 and stored in isopropyl.

I feel like either "The SCP-XXXX instance…" or "All the SCP-XXXX instances…" would work better here; really emphasise that there's not just one SCP but a whole host of them, y'know?

is not conducive to healthy function

something about 'healthy function' feels really odd here; it feels weirdly dehumanising and I'm not sure whether that's good or not?

Due to global and regional disparities in access to and quality of healthcare for trans and non-binary people, as well as the social capability for such individuals to be open about their identity, detection of SCP-XXXX activity is difficult.

Part of me wonders whether explicitly mentioning webcrawlers and social media here would be a good idea but I think this is fine?

including a long prehensile tail and a segmented anatomic structure.

SCP-XXXX is equipped with a jawless, toothed mouth and four hooklike claws on its underdeveloped appendages. Instances have been recorded to reach lengths greater than 0.4 meters.

I can't quite put my finger on why; but something about this flow feels iffy? I wonder whether moving the 'greater than 0.4meters' to a footnote after 'enlarged' would help?

It's possibly that this is the first time you mention 'instances' or the repetition of sentences starting with 'SCP-XXXX' being broken this way is a little jarring but I'm not sure.

Analysis has shown SCP-XXXX to be genetically identical to humans.

This feels…iffy; 'humans' feels like an overly broad thing for 'genetically identical' to work since like two humans can be relatively genetically different? I wonder whether specificity would help here: are they genetically identical to their host? To one specific human?

These subjects, hereby referred to as SCP-XXXX-1

It feels odd to have a -1 but not have anything in the ConProcs relating to it

is sleeping. it then makes its way to offspring of SCP-XXXX-1 in proximity.

missing capital; and ending on 'in proximity' feels like it's missing a noun (like, in that, it's implied you mean 'in proximity to -1' but the construction feels iffy cos there's no explicit thing saying that); and also feels vague; perhaps tying the 'travel up to a kilometer' line in here would work better instead of having it in the next sentence?

SCP-XXXX will attach itself to offspring of SCP-XXXX-1 that identify as transgender or non-binary

'identify' feels odd here: it kinda implies that a) people who aren't trans but identify as can be affected and b) people who are trans but don't identify as such can't be affected and I wonder whether just saying 'offspring of -1 that are' would be better?

SCP-XXXX does not feed on SCP-XXXX-2 directly.

This feels a little weirdly placed right now: it's kinda mentioned in passing in the middle of a paragraph, but the idea of feeding isn't touched on more for like…two, large paragraphs more, and so it feels like perhaps it'd work best just before the "SCP-XXXX is thought to feed on positive attention paid to…." sentence?

However, the perceived appearance of SCP-XXXX-2 will differ from their actual pre-exposure appearance in multiple ways. These inconsistencies mimic the secondary sexual characteristics of the sex assigned to SCP-XXXX-2 at birth, as well as non-genetic traits stereotypically associated with that sex by the culture of the subject observing SCP-XXXX-2.

This section, and the rest of the paragraph it's in, feels…like it uses a lot of words to not say a lot: the dense, clinical tone feels like it doesn't setup a very evocative image of the transformation. I feel like perhaps trimming down the list of alterations a little, and perhaps mentioning a few examples might convey this more evocatively but it might be hard to get the examples to feel right here.

If SCP-XXXX-2 possesses a chosen name different from the name given to them at birth, they will become unable to pronounce it.

Does this apply if they meet someone else using the name? I guess this isn't fully a critique so much as me wondering whether this has much larger scale impacts than intended?

[-] Line By Line

item.title: First SCP Draft: Re: First SCP Draft
item.content:encoded: Well, we already know what the best-case scenario is here: Ben improves on his own and moves beyond his alternate selves. With that in mind, what would you say is the worst-case scenario for him here? Thinking about that might help us identify some stakes that could be heightened.
